item.title: A Custom Hardware Accelerator for Softmax Function With Parallel Online Normalization
item.description: Softmax computation in transformer-based LLM/SLM models commonly relies on online normalization to ensure numerical stability while reducing memory access cycles. However, conventional online formulations introduce loop-carried dependencies that result in serialization, restricting scalable spatial parallelism, and efficient wide-datapath realization in hardware implementations. This article presents a custom Softmax hardware accelerator (CSHA) based on an algorithm–architecture codesigned parallel online normalization framework. The proposed algorithm reformulates sequential online normalization into a parallel streaming-compatible structure while preserving numerical stability and memory efficiency, thereby enabling scalable datapath parallelism. All core computational units—maximum detection, exponential approximation, reduction trees, multiplication, and logarithmic computation—are circuit-optimized and synthesized in a 90 nm CMOS process to evaluate area, power, and delay tradeoffs. The CSHA employs a fully pipelined fixed-point architecture designed for accuracy-aware hardware efficiency. System-level validation is performed by replacing the floating-point Softmax in a pretrained BERT model with the proposed implementation, demonstrating less than 1% accuracy degradation across GLUE tasks and the SQuAD dataset. Field programmable gate array (FPGA) deployment on a Zynq-7000 SoC further verifies functional correctness and dynamic sequence-length configurability, eliminating redundant padded Softmax computation. By integrating algorithm reformulation with circuit-level optimization, the proposed CSHA provides an efficient and scalable oSftmax solution suitable for low-power, high-throughput inference systems.

item.title: TetraPIXA: A High-Performance and Resource-Efficient Accelerator for Pillar and Voxel Feature Networks in 3-D Point Cloud Object Detection
item.description: Point cloud data (PCD) acquired using 3-D sensing technologies offer unique advantages over 2-D camera images in applications such as robotics and autonomous driving. In particular, voxel- and pillar-based point cloud neural networks (PNNs) have demonstrated strong performance in large-scale outdoor 3-D object detection scenarios. However, due to the irregular, sparse, and unordered nature of PCD, prior approaches, including GPU-based solutions, struggle to process such data efficiently and typically require substantial hardware resources. To address these challenges, this article proposes TetraPIXA, a high-performance and resource-efficient accelerator that employs a unified architecture supporting both voxel feature network (VFN) and pillar feature network (PFN), which serve as the critical preprocessing stages where these challenges primarily arise. By exploiting spatial locality, TetraPIXA enables independent operation of multiple cores, thereby achieving effective data-level parallelism. In addition, temporal locality is leveraged to significantly reduce the latency of time-consuming and exhaustive pillar-voxel (PV) operations without introducing additional hardware overhead. For feature encoding (FE), which involves compute-intensive multiply–accumulate (MAC) operations, TetraPIXA incorporates a resource-aware parallel and pipelined (RAPP) architecture in conjunction with spatial locality to achieve resource-efficient acceleration. TetraPIXA was implemented and evaluated on an FPGA platform and achieves up to $39.9\times $ speedup over prior works with a power consumption of only 1.2 W, while maintaining the detection accuracy of the full-precision baseline.

item.title: ME-MoD: Algorithm-Hardware-Dataflow Co-Design for Memory Efficient Mixture-of-Depth-Based Vision Transformer Accelerator
item.description: Transformers outperform traditional neural networks but face high computational and memory costs, limiting edge device deployment. Although many hardware accelerators aim to address this, the original Transformer structure still restricts the optimization effect. A recent breakthrough, mixture-of-depths (MoDs), employs conditional computation and effectively reduces the computational complexity of large language models, providing a valuable opportunity for designing an efficient hardware accelerator. However, when applied to vision transformers, MoD suffers from accuracy degradation and excessive external memory access (EMA). Therefore, this article presents ME-MoD, the first memory-efficient MoD-based vision transformer inference accelerator, leveraging the idea of reordering and algorithm-hardware-dataflow codesign. Algorithmically, distribution adjustment forward (DAF) and routing decision forward (RDF) techniques restore accuracy and alleviate memory access costs through token reordering. Architecturally, a LayerNorm-Routing (L-R) fusion module and a token reordering and sequential recording module enhance computational efficiency while minimizing memory overhead. In addition, a token-stationary layer fusion dataflow and an on-chip dynamic memory module are designed, which further optimizes the EMA caused by the intermediate results of interlayer computation of valid tokens routed by MoD. With negligible accuracy loss, our ME-MoD accelerator achieves $1.62\times $ inference speed up, eliminates 46.5% of the external memory bandwidth requirement and 45.2% of energy consumption compared with standard MoD. It achieves 23.6 TOPS/W energy efficiency, which is $4.02\times $ improvements compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) designs.

item.title: Workload-Aware Compressor Tree Design Automation With Statistical Calibration for Efficient AI Accelerators
item.description: A compressor tree is an essential building block of multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) units, hierarchically reducing multiple partial sums without immediate carry propagation. This article introduces a workload-aware compressor tree synthesis framework that aligns model-level noise tolerance with hardware-level arithmetic design to enable statistically guided MAC in artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators. Unlike conventional compressor trees that rely on uniform approximation policies, the proposed approach derives an allowable error budget by analyzing noise–accuracy behavior and profiling workload-specific bit-pattern distributions, revealing that most significant bit (MSB) regions are biased toward high-Hamming-weight values, such as all-ones and near-all-ones cases. Guided by these statistics, the framework automatically selects among exact and approximate compressors from a characterization library, and incorporates a pattern-accurate 6:3 compressor designed to minimize MSB-sensitive error while preserving hardware efficiency. This unified flow generates compressor trees that remain compliant with model-derived accuracy constraints while significantly reducing cost. Fabricated in a commercial 28 nm process, the resulting designs improve delay and power by up to 15%–25% across diverse convolutional neural network (CNN) and Transformer models, achieving 14–27 TOPS/W while maintaining only 0.07% average inference accuracy degradation. These results highlight that workload-calibrated accumulation is a critical optimization axis for modern AI accelerators and demonstrate the value of statistically specialized compressor structures for domain-specific edge inference accelerator deployments.

item.title: A 22-nm End-to-End Edge--AI Processor With Booth-Value-Confined Acceleration and Hardware-Aware Layer-Wise Model Deployment
item.description: Edge devices capable of running artificial intelligence (AI) applications have seen a surge in demand for energy-efficient and high-throughput computation. In this study, a 22-nm edge–AI processor, incorporating an accelerator with error-free Booth-value-confined (BVC) multiprecision (MP) multiplier and near-memory computing (NMC), is introduced to accelerate neural networks (NNs). It has the following three major features. First, a BVC MP multiplier based on radix-8 Booth (R8B) is introduced to reduce computation complexity by prohibiting the “±3” cases and support error-free training on GPU without accuracy loss originating from the mismatch between training and deployment. A PE is built based on this multiplier for parallel computation with 82% power reduction and 70% area reduction. Second, the proposed NMC-friendly data flow supports efficient data reuse and hence reduces off-chip memory traffic. The data flow supports data reuse of up to 16 times, matching the number of PEs and enabling regular read and write patterns. Third, a hardware-aware layer-wise model deployment approach is proposed with a memory space contiguity-aware (MSCA) model reshape strategy, and a hardware-aware NN splitting and scheduling algorithm. The proposed MSCA strategy maximizes burst access, and the proposed algorithm achieves efficient computation with high data reuse and low memory access. This deployment approach can achieve a reduction in memory access latency of 16.6%–32.0%. Measurements on a 22-nm test chip demonstrate a peak power efficiency of 33.98 TOPS/W under synthetic full-PE-utilization conditions, while achieving 12.92–29.11 TOPS/W for end-to-end NN inference on DarkNet19, VGG16, ViT-Tiny, and ResNet34.

item.title: 7T SRAM Macro Supporting 2W/2R Adjacent Dual-Row Access for Enhanced Memory Bandwidth and Energy Efficiency
item.description: This article proposes a 7T static random access memory (SRAM) macro using an adjacent dual-row simultaneous access (DRSA) scheme based on an independent single-ended bitline control (ISBC) technique. Using this technique, the SRAM enables simultaneous dual-write (2W) or dual-read (2R) operations on two adjacent rows within a single cycle, thereby achieving a $2\times $ bandwidth improvement over conventional single-row access (SRA) SRAMs. Accordingly, the proposed DRSA scheme significantly improves energy efficiency and latency by reducing the number of access cycles required for a given workload. Designed in a 28-nm CMOS process, the 4-Kb 7T SRAM macro demonstrates a total active energy of 0.163 pJ/access/bit in DRSA mode, which is $0.75\times $ that of a conventional SRA SRAM.

item.title: HierCIM: A 16-Kb SRAM-Based Digital CIM Macro With Hierarchical Adder-Tree Accumulation for Edge CNN Inference
item.description: The growing demand for efficient deep-learning inference on edge platforms requires hardware that is both energy-efficient and practically implementable. This work presents a 16-Kb all-digital static random-access memory (SRAM)-based compute-in-memory (CIM) macro for low-bit CNN inference, featuring a hierarchical adder-tree-based accumulation architecture. The design integrates a nor-enabled SRAM compute cell, column-wise rearrangement network, sparsity-aware compression, and multistage hierarchical accumulation within a 64-bank $64 \,\, \times \,\, 4$ architecture, enabling scalable bit-serial processing and utilization-aware mapping. Implemented in 65-nm CMOS, the macro achieves 8.19 TOPS effective throughput at 1.0 V and a peak energy efficiency of 586 TOPS/W at 0.9 V under practical operating conditions. Hardware-compatible CNN mapping is demonstrated using LeNet-5, VGG-8, and ResNet-8. The design achieves 98.1% and 72.3% accuracy on MNIST and CIFAR-10, respectively, with 1-bit activations and 4-bit weights, while 4-bit configurations on deeper networks show only 3%–4% degradation from FP32 baselines. CNN inference is evaluated using a hardware-compatible post-training quantization (PTQ) flow without retraining. These results demonstrate that the proposed SRAM-CIM architecture provides an efficient and scalable accumulation solution with a practical tradeoff among throughput, energy efficiency, and implementability for edge-oriented deep neural network (DNN) inference.

item.title: EVA: Efficient Token Compression Co-Optimization With Heterogeneous CIM Architecture for Video LLM Acceleration
item.description: Video large language models (VLLMs) enable powerful multimodal reasoning but face severe efficiency challenges on edge devices due to the massive computational and memory demands caused by lengthy video-token sequences. Existing methods struggle to efficiently compress spatiotemporally redundant tokens while minimizing DRAM access overhead during inference. In this work, we propose EVA, a co-designed algorithm–hardware framework for accelerating VLLMs. At the algorithm level, we introduce an efficient training-free token compression (ETC) method that combines greedy temporal segmentation (GTS) to adaptively partition frames by content similarity, with diversity spatiotemporal compression (DSC) to retain semantically rich tokens from both static and dynamic regions. The method is plug-and-play, requires no retraining, and employs sign similarity to enable hardware-friendly computing at scale. At the hardware level, we design a heterogeneous accelerator integrating a lightweight token compression engine (TCE), a computing-in-memory (CIM) engine for in situ execution of linear layers, and a reconfigurable digital attention engine with hardware-specialized attention computation and an interleaved pipeline dataflow. Across multiple models and video benchmarks, EVA preserves accuracy under aggressive token reduction and delivers substantial efficiency gains. Notably, on LLaVA-OneVision-7B, EVA compresses 90% of video tokens while maintaining 97.8% of the original accuracy. EVA achieves up to $10.3\times $ speedup and $47.4\times $ energy reduction compared to GPU, and achieves up to $3.8\times $ speedup over prior specialized accelerators, demonstrating a practical path toward scalable VLLM inference on resource-constrained devices.

item.title: GFRA: A High-Utilization Grain-Fused Reconfigurable Architecture for Coarse-Grained and Fine-Grained Applications
item.description: The evolving computational tasks impose higher demands on hardware resource utilization. Coarse-grained reconfigurable architectures (CGRAs), owing to their high flexibility and energy efficiency, exhibit significant potential in addressing these demands. However, when CGRAs handle hybrid coarse-grained (CG) and fine-grained (FG) operations—such as CG arithmetic operations like multiply-accumulate and FG operations like and/or—the processing elements (PEs) cannot be fully utilized for CG computation because some PEs are allocated to FG tasks. This results in low PE resource utilization and further limits the parallel acceleration capability of CGRAs. To address this, we propose a high-utilization grain-fused reconfigurable architecture (GFRA) that integrates Boolean processor (BP) technology. The GFRA architecture, incorporating Boolean processor technology, is implemented to optimize CG and FG computations, thereby improving CG resource utilization and parallel acceleration capability. The core idea of GFRA is that CGRA offloads FG computations to Boolean processors to achieve parallel acceleration. Specifically, dedicated computing units for CG and FG operations, optimized interconnection paths, and a hierarchical management approach for information flow are proposed, enhancing the architecture’s efficiency in handling control flow, configuration flow, and data flow for hybrid-grained tasks. Compared with representative CGRAs, GFRA achieves an average CG resource utilization of 90.4%, an average normalized speedup improvement of 48.5%, and an average normalized execution time reduction of 45.7%, and demonstrates the best performance in cryptographic tasks.

item.title: Routing-Aware In Situ Diagnosis of PDN- and Configuration-Induced Delay Signatures in SRAM-Based FPGAs
item.description: Timing degradation in static random-access memory (SRAM)-based field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) can arise from multiple physical mechanisms, including power-distribution-network (PDN) stress and configuration-induced routing perturbations. Although both appear as the delay increases, their spatial and statistical signatures differ. This article presents a routing-aware in situ diagnosis framework that observes timing behavior at selected switch-matrix-accessible routing nodes during operation. The method combines nonintrusive delay taps (DTs), phase-swept sampling, and centralized statistical analysis to extract BER-versus-phase timing signatures from tapped routing signals. Experimental results on an Xilinx/AMD XCZU7EV FPGA show that PDN-induced effects produce broadly correlated delay shifts with limited variance growth, whereas configuration-induced routing perturbations produce localized, topology-dependent delay increases and stronger dispersion. Spatial correlation analysis further separates these mechanisms through their distinct correlation decay patterns. The proposed framework is intended for comparative diagnosis and spatial characterization of routing-observable timing degradation rather than complete path coverage or immediate timing-failure protection. The implementation uses lightweight instrumentation and scales linearly with the number of monitored routing locations, making it suitable for targeted in-fabric timing diagnosis in deployed FPGA systems.

item.title: Hardware--Algorithm Co-Design for Efficient Bit-Serial Acceleration of Lightweight CNNs With Standard and Depthwise Convolutions on FPGA
item.description: Bit-serial computation (BSC) is attractive for field-programmable gated array (FPGA)-based convolutional neural network (CNN) acceleration because it naturally supports mixed-precision quantization and bit-level sparse computation. However, MobileNetV2-like lightweight CNNs contain standard convolution (SC) and depthwise separable convolution (DSC) layers, which impose different bottlenecks on conventional BSC. SC layers provide sufficient input-channel parallelism but suffer from redundant weight-bit computation, whereas DSC layers have only one input channel and cause severe utilization mismatch with fixed input-channel-parallel bit-serial MAC units. To address these issues, this paper proposes an operator-aware hardware–algorithm co-design framework. For SC layers, mixed-precision quantization (MPQ) and column-based bit-level sparsity (CBBLS) are jointly adopted to reduce effective weight-bit computation. For DSC layers, a dataflow-reconfigurable bit-serial MAC (DR-BSMAC) is proposed to improve hardware utilization. Implemented on an Xilinx VCU118 FPGA at 300 MHz, the proposed accelerator achieves 806.5 GOPS on MobileNetV2 with only 1.48% top-1 accuracy loss on ImageNet, providing $2.39\times $ overall throughput improvement over the 8-bit baseline. The same framework also achieves 581.9 GOPS and $2.27\times $ speedup on EfficientNet-B0. Compared with state-of-the-art accelerators, our design improves equivalent LUT efficiency and energy efficiency by up to $7.03\times $ and $4.74\times $ on MobileNetV2 and by up to $16.50\times $ and $4.49\times $ on EfficientNet-B0, respectively. The DR-BSMAC RTL is publicly available at https://github.com/haden-01/DR-BSMAC.git

item.title: Low-Power FPGA Implementation of Twin Support Vector Machine-Based Epileptic Seizure Detection Algorithm
item.description: In neurological research, detecting epileptic seizures is the most crucial task using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals for clinical applications. Implementing a conventional support vector machine (SVM) for seizure detection is computationally intensive for real-time applications. The twin SVM (TSVM), a variant of SVM, along with the sequential minimal optimization (SMO) algorithm, is appropriate for hardware acceleration as it provides reduced computational complexity with better classification performance. In order to detect seizures in real-time using EEG signals, this article presents the field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based implementation of the TSVM framework accelerated using the SMO algorithm for efficient real-time seizure detection on an Xilinx Virtex 7 FPGA board. The proposed framework follows a software–hardware (S/H) co-design methodology, in which EEG preprocessing, normalization, feature extraction, and feature selection are implemented in MATLAB, whereas the SMO optimization engine and TSVM classifier are implemented on FPGA hardware, thereby achieving better computation with minimal power consumption through efficient arithmetic operations and parallel processing. The proposed design is validated on benchmark EEG datasets from the CHB-MIT dataset, achieving high classification accuracy and low latency when implemented with a linear kernel TSVM. Besides that, it uses $1.6\times $ less power compared to the earlier performed implementation in prior work using SVM. A more accurate diagnosis through TSVM may lead to better treatment and patient care. The development of TSVM and SMO algorithms is expected to improve seizure detection and treatment. It will, in turn, allow for more efficient and effective medical solutions.

item.title: New Side-Channel Vulnerabilities in Resource-Constrained Montgomery Ladder Scalar Multiplication Based on Projective Coordinates
item.description: Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) primitives over prime fields are integral to many security protocols due to their compact key sizes and strong security. Scalar multiplication is a complex operation at the core of ECC algorithms. Scalar multiplication is often implemented following the Montgomery ladder to mitigate side-channel power analysis risks due to its uniform execution pattern. This work introduces new side-channel vulnerabilities on the ladder when facing resource-constrained hardware requirements for implementing potential projective coordinate formulations. The new vulnerability is exploited through mounting a full-stack horizontal power analysis (HPA) attack using as few as a single power trace in some cases.

item.title: A Tiny Neuromorphic Processor Enabling On-Chip Spike-Based Learning for Edge Intelligent System
item.description: Neuromorphic processors deploying spiking neural networks (SNNs) hold great potential for edge intelligence applications. However, achieving high accuracy, high throughput, and highly energy-efficient on-chip learning under limited energy and resource budgets remains a critical challenge. To address this, we propose a tiny neuromorphic architecture to support a fully spike-based backpropagation learning algorithm tailored for a lightweight two-layer SNN aiming at edge scenarios. To enhance processing efficiency, this architecture tightly couples control and data flows, and features fully spike-based inference and learning. Furthermore, we propose a structured weight mapping scheme that satisfies different parallel memory access patterns during forward and backward passes, and introduce a group-based event-driven paradigm to exploit spike sparsity. A prototype was implemented on a very-low-cost Xilinx Zynq-7010 FPGA device. It achieved high on-chip learning accuracies comparable to state-of-the-art works across multiple benchmark datasets, while delivering a throughput of 2269/9082 frames/s and an energy efficiency of 56/ $14~\mu $ J/image for learning/inferring MNIST images, which outperforms existing approaches and shows its potential for wide deployments in extreme edge intelligence scenarios.

item.title: A 2-kHz BW 89.2-dB SNDR 100-dB SFDR Σ–Δ DAC for Precision Instruments
item.description: This brief presents a $\Sigma $ – $\Delta $ digital-to-analog converter (DAC) for precision instruments. To enhance the power efficiency, a direct-charge-transfer (DCT) DAC is proposed. In addition, an analog smoothing filter is integrated to suppress the high-frequency noise, enhancing the quality of the output signal. Compared with the traditional filter off-chip strategy, on-chip active filters enable a better suppression of out-of-band noise and harmonics. This work adopts a co-design approach in which the on-chip active filter and the data-weighted averaging (DWA)-DCT path are jointly optimized to suppress switching glitches and out-of-band noise, thereby enabling high-precision performance. Fabricated in a 180-nm CMOS process, the proposed $\Sigma $ – $\Delta $ DAC occupies an area of 0.43 mm2 and consumes 3.68 mW from a 3.3-V supply. On condition that the sampling frequency (f ${}_{\mathrm {s}}$ ) is set to be 256 kS/s, the DAC achieves a maximum signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 89.2 dB and a spurious-free-dynamic-range (SFDR) of 100 dB over 2-kHz bandwidth. The maximum differential nonlinearity error (DNL) is 0.36 LSB, indicating no missing code for static applications.

item.title: Metastability-Based Time-Gain-Enhanced Voltage-to-Time Converter With Time-Offset Calibration for Time-Domain Applications
item.description: Voltage-to-time converters (VTCs) utilizing metastability are widely used in high-speed applications, where the VTC gain is critical because it affects input sensitivity and the sampling margin. However, existing methods for high VTC gain often introduce additional challenges. To address this issue, this brief introduces a metastability-based double-tail VTC incorporating a cross-coupled nMOS pair in the dynamic preamplifier. This structure increases the clock (CLK)-to-Q delay at small input voltages while minimizing the delay increase at large inputs, thereby enhancing the VTC gain. In addition, a binary-weighted $g_{m}$ control time-offset calibration circuit compensates for delay variations caused by device mismatch and process, voltage, and temperature variations, and a CLK-separated comparator structure eliminates short-circuit current paths for power saving. Postlayout simulations in 65-nm CMOS technology at a 0.8-V VDD show that the VTC gain increased from 0.24 to 0.449 ps/mV.

item.title: An Energy-Efficient GPS Acquisition Macro Using Accurate Approximate SRAM-PIM for Low-Power GNSS Applications
item.description: The signal acquisition, one of the most computation-intensive stages in global navigation satellite system (GNSS) receivers, dominates both power consumption and area overhead. To reduce global positioning system (GPS) acquisition latency and improve receiver energy efficiency, this brief proposes an energy-efficient GPS acquisition macro based on accurate/approximate static random-access memory (SRAM) processing-in-memory (PIM). The proposed design performs parallel code-phase and Doppler-frequency searches through PIM-based convolution and discrete Fourier transform (DFT) operations, eliminating the need for a real-time coarse acquisition (C/A)-code generator, thereby reducing data movement and acquisition power. An accurate/approximate dual-mode computing strategy is introduced to enable a flexible tradeoff between acquisition probability and energy efficiency under different signal environments. Moreover, a flexible GPS acquisition workflow supporting both convolution and convolution-DFT algorithms is developed to improve the generality of the architecture, thereby enhancing architectural flexibility. Fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process, the prototype chip achieves an average energy efficiency of 285.4 TOPS/W at 0.55 V in the convolution mode, delivering a $2.67\times $ improvement over the state of the art and demonstrating its efficiency and scalability for low-power, highly integrated satellite navigation and positioning applications.

item.title: A 90.9-dB SNDR Fourth-Order Fully Passive Bandpass Current-Integrating Noise-Shaping SAR Light-to-Digital Converter
item.description: This brief presents a fully passive fourth-order bandpass (BP) light-to-digital converter (LDC) using a current-integrating (CI) noise-shaping (NS) successive approximation register (SAR) architecture for optical sensor interfaces and BP digitization. The proposed BP LDC achieves a sharp in-band noise suppression of −28 dB with a single-channel CI NS-SAR quantizer with passive gain and direct “ $z\to -z^{2}$ ” transformation. Inheriting the advantages of the CI-SAR architecture, it offers inherent antialiasing, dynamic range (DR) extension, and minimizes the analog front-end (AFE) duty cycle, achieving high power efficiency for direct light-to-digital conversion. A prototype, fabricated in a 180-nm process, achieves a 90.9-dB signal-to-noise-distortion ratio (SNDR) and a 107.2-dB DR in a 500-Hz bandwidth. The power consumption is 35.41- $\mu $ W, resulting in a FoMSNDR of 162.4 dB and a FoMDR of 178.7 dB without a separate transimpedance amplifier.

item.title: CLPA: A Clustering-Based Low-Power Accelerator for Energy-Efficient Matrix Multiplication
item.description: Efficient matrix multiplication is pivotal to minimizing the energy consumption associated with large language model (LLM) inference. In this work, we propose the bit-constrained Hamming clustering (BCHC) algorithm, an innovative approach designed to enhance energy efficiency in matrix multiplication. By imposing constraints on Hamming distance and position, the BCHC algorithm increases bit-level sparsity to $1.71\times \sim$ $ 1.78\times $ . Based on the BCHC algorithm, we design a sign decoder (SDecoder) to reduce the additional external memory access (EMA) and clustering-based processing element (CBPE) to leverage the bit-level sparsity after clustering. At last, we propose a low-power accelerator, named clustering-based low-power attention calculation accelerator (CLPA). Tested on multiple LLM benchmarks, CLPA achieves $2.05\times $ to $2.19\times $ GOPS/W improvement compared to Stripes and $1.20\times $ to $1.27\times $ GOPS/W improvement compared to Cambricon-C in energy efficiency.

item.title: A 6.3--18.4 GHz I/Q Receiver With RF and LO Path Reconfigurability for 6G FR3 Applications in 22-nm FD-SOI
item.description: This article presents a 6.3–18.4 GHz in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) direct down-conversion receiver featuring reconfigurability in both the radio frequency (RF) and local oscillator (LO) paths. The receiver comprises a multi-band reconfigurable RF front-end, double-balanced passive I/Q mixers, an I/Q LO generation network with a tunable I/Q vector correction circuit, and wideband baseband amplifiers. The integrated reconfigurable RF front end enables optimized performance across different bands. The LO drivers and the polyphase filter (PPF) are co-designed to maximize the overall LO chain voltage gain with low power consumption. Also, the tunable LO I/Q vector correction circuit is implemented at the LO output drivers to minimize I/Q phase error over a wide frequency range while introducing minimal additional voltage loss. Fabricated in 22-nm CMOS fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) technology, the receiver achieves a measured 3-dB conversion gain (CG) of 20 dB at 6.3–18.4 GHz, a noise figure (NF) of 2.4–5.3 dB, an image-rejection ratio (IRR) exceeding 40 dB, and an input 1-dB compression point (IP1dB) greater than –26 dBm, with an average power consumption of 79 mW. The receiver targets high-data-rate 6G frequency range 3 (FR3) wireless communication applications.

item.title: Omnidirectional Multi-Transmitter Wireless Power Transfer System With Integrated Coupling Coefficient Sensor
item.description: A 6.78-MHz multi-transmitter wireless power transfer (WPT) system that allows relaxed alignment power transfer is proposed. The coupling coefficient ( $k$ ) between each transmitting coil and the receiving coil is analyzed. By using a novel integrated coupling coefficient sensor ( $k$ -sensor), transmitter $i$ ( $TX_{i}$ ) is selectively activated based on the magnitude of $k_{i}$ , and the phase of the received current is duly adjusted to avoid current cancellation to increase the system power transfer efficiency ( $\eta _{SYS}$ ). Power control is implemented on an integrated circuit (IC) fabricated using a 0.18- ${\mu }$ m CMOS process with 3.3-V devices. The WPT system consists of one receiver (RX) coil and a $2~{\times }~2$ transmitter (TX) coil array driven by the proposed IC. Eight RX coil positions were evaluated to assess the performance of the WPT system. Experimental results show that, compared with the multi-TX WPT system without using the $k$ -sensor, the best improvement occurred when the RX coil was positioned perpendicular to the TX coils, with $\eta _{SYS}$ increased from 0.3% to 63.7%, and delivered power rose from 3 mW to 2 W. Performance enhancement was observed for most cases.

item.title: An H-Band Continuous Broadband RF-Domain Quadrature Receiver Using a Harmonic-Enhanced LO Generator in 65-nm CMOS
item.description: This article presents an $H$ -band CMOS receiver chipset that covers a wide frequency range of 228–324 GHz, supporting the entire band of IEEE Std. 802.15.3d. The proposed receiver employs an RF-domain quadrature mixer-first architecture to alleviate the design burden of quadrature local oscillator (LO) signal generation in $H$ -band, which is beneficial for achieving a large bandwidth. Moreover, a harmonic-enhanced $\times 12$ frequency multiplier chain (FMC) is used as an LO generator with improved bandwidth, output power ( ${P} _{\textrm {out}}$ ), and harmonic rejection ratio (HRR) to support wideband performance of the receiver. In the FMC, a double-balanced self-mixing (DBSM) tripler is proposed to achieve a superior fundamental rejection ratio, and a dual-mode harmonic-tuning doubler is proposed to enhance the output power of the FMC in $H$ -band. The receiver and the standalone FMC were fabricated in a 65-nm CMOS technology. Measurement results show that the FMC achieves a peak ${P} _{\textrm {out}}$ of 4.27 dBm and a 3-dB bandwidth of 218–292 GHz. Besides, the HRR of the FMC is better than 26 dBc from 228 to 310 GHz. Moreover, the proposed receiver demonstrates a wideband performance of 228–324 GHz with a minimum noise figure (NF) of 22.1 dB. The receiver also supports 16-QAM/64-QAM/128-QAM modulation in various channels of IEEE Std. 802.15.3d, and achieves a data rate of 40 Gb/s with 16-QAM modulation in Channel 57.

item.title: A 2.88-pJ/bit 830.7-MHz High-Efficiency OOK Transmitter With Pulse-Driven and Energy-Recycled MEMS Oscillator
item.description: This work presents an 830.7-MHz on-off-keying (OOK) transmitter (TX) based on a MEMS oscillator employing pulse-driven and energy-recycling techniques. To improve system efficiency, stacked inverter-based power amplifier (PA) is utilized, while energy-recycling from the top stacked PA is exploited to power the oscillator. An on-chip 2.7:1 transformer is designed to boost the load impedance seen by the PA, thereby maximizing PA efficiency without the need for an external matching network. The proposed TX is fabricated in a TSMC 40-nm CMOS process and occupies a die area of 1.73 mm2. The MEMS oscillator consumes only $176.5~{\mu }$ W while achieving a phase noise of −118.2 dBc/Hz at a 100-kHz offset. Under continuous operation, the TX supports a data rate of 100 Mb/s, resulting in an energy efficiency of 2.88 pJ/bit at an output power of −15 dBm. By adopting a duty-cycling ratio of 4%, the TX consumes only $13.8~{\mu }$ W at a data rate of 3 Mb/s, which is at least $7{\times }$ lower than that of other reported works.

item.title: A Low-Jitter Fractional-N Sampling PLL With Voltage-Domain Quantization-Error Cancellation Using a Nonlinearity-Replication Technique
item.description: This work presents a low-jitter, low-fractional-spur fractional- $N$ digital sampling phase-locked loop (SPLL) that generates output frequencies from 10.4 to 11.8 GHz. Conventional fractional- $N$ PLLs employ a digital-to-time converter (DTC) to cancel the quantization error (Q-error) of the delta-sigma modulator ( $\Delta \Sigma $ M). To address the nonlinearity (NL) of the DTC, i.e., NLDTC, which degrades the rms jitter and spur performance, previous designs have employed either a digital pre-distortion (DPD) technique that requires significant hardware overhead or a highly linear DTC that inevitably increases design complexity. In contrast, this work presents a replica-NL digital-to-analog converter (RNL-DAC) that intrinsically replicates the NL profile of the sampling phase detector (SPD), thereby naturally canceling the $\Delta \Sigma $ M Q-error with minimal design resources. This work also presents a complementary voltage comparator (VC) that accommodates a wide range of input voltages, thereby maintaining high sampling gain for low in-band phase-noise (PN). The proposed fractional- $N$ SPLL was fabricated in a 40-nm CMOS process and consumed 15.3 mW while generating an 11.1-GHz output signal from a 150-MHz reference. The measured rms jitter and fractional spur were 76 fs and −65 dBc, respectively, at a fractional- $N$ frequency near 11.1 GHz, demonstrating an excellent jitter-power figure of merit (FoM ${}_{\mathrm {JIT}}$ ) despite its simple architecture.

item.title: A 6.8--14-GHz Ring-Based Sampling-PLL Achieving 69.3-fs Jitter Under 50-mV Supply Noise
item.description: This article presents a type-III wide-bandwidth ring-oscillator-based analog phase-locked loop (PLL) optimized for low-jitter performance in noisy supply environments. The design uses an 812.5-MHz reference frequency and a high-gain sampling phase detector to achieve a closed-loop bandwidth over 100 MHz, effectively reducing the intrinsic phase noise of the ring oscillator. To improve the voltage-controlled ring oscillator (VCRO) tuning range and supply noise rejection, the PLL includes an additional integrator and an NMOS-based voltage regulator. Fabricated in a 22-nm FinFET process, the proposed integer-N PLL achieves a 13-GHz output with an integrated (10 kHz–100 MHz) jitter of 69.3 fs and supports a continuous tuning range from 6.8 to 14 GHz with an eight-phase output. The supply regulation scheme enhances noise immunity by 31.4 dB, keeping worst case spurious tones below −54 dBc under a 50-mV $\rm _{pp}$ sinusoidal supply ripple, with minimal jitter degradation (69.3 versus 67.5 fs). The combination of a wide tuning range, low jitter, and strong supply noise suppression makes the proposed PLL ideal for high-speed clock generation in serial links over 100 Gb/s.

item.title: A Low-Jitter, Energy-Efficient 6/12-GHz Phase Interpolator With 0.18 mW/GHz in 65-nm CMOS
item.description: This article presents a novel low-power, low-noise phase interpolator (PI) with high resolution designed for diverse applications such as local clock generation in clock data recovery (CDR) to sample time-interleaved analog-to-digital-converter (TI-ADC) and baseband delay beamforming. The proposed PI, implemented in 65-nm CMOS, utilizes a ramp signal with constant slope and swing, whose DC level is dynamically modulated by the input code. This design enables high-speed operation with a power efficiency of 0.18 mW/GHz and reduced noise levels. Integration of a four-stage injection-locked ring oscillator (RO) at the final stage eliminates the need for an input delay-locked loop (DLL), duty-cycle corrector (DCC), and output quadrature generator. This innovative design simultaneously generates a 4-phase output at 6 GHz with an IQ error below 0.9° and a 2-phase output at 12 GHz. The fabricated PI covers the full 360° range while consuming only 2.2 mW and occupying a compact 0.025 mm2. It also achieves an rms jitter of just 68 fs, with differential non-linearity (DNL) and integral non-linearity (INL) measured at 0.9 and 1.9 LSB, respectively.

item.title: A 16-MHz CMOS RC Frequency Reference Achieving Accuracies of ±125 ppm From −40 °C to 85 °C and −560/+580 ppm After Accelerated Aging
item.description: This article presents a low-power, high-accuracy CMOS RC frequency reference featuring a capacitively modulated RC time constant (CMT) generation and a die-to-die error removal (DDER) technique for precise frequency generation with a low-calibration cost. Unlike resistive trimming, the temperature dependence of the on-chip resistor is compensated by a $\Delta \Sigma $ -modulated capacitance in the proposed CMT with a trimming resolution up to 6 ppm while the proposed DDER further eliminates the residual die-to-die error (DDE) due to process spread in high-order batch calibration. Fabricated in a standard 0.18- $\mu $ m CMOS process, the 16-MHz prototype occupies an active area of 0.1 mm2 and consumes $120~\mu $ W when operating from a 1.8-V supply, achieving an energy efficiency of 7.5 pJ/cycle. Measurement results from 15 samples of the same batch demonstrate that the proposed DDER technique achieves a frequency accuracy improvement exceeding ±100 ppm compared with when DDER disabled, while maintaining an average frequency inaccuracy of ±125 ppm across the $- 40~^{\circ }$ C to $85~^{\circ }$ C operating temperature range. When further combining pre-aging with the proposed CMT and DDER techniques, the proposed frequency reference achieves a frequency accuracy of −560/+580 ppm after accelerated aging, while maintaining comparable or better jitter and long-term stability performance among CMOS RC-time-constant-based frequency References.

item.title: A Third-Harmonic-Enhanced Triple-Push DCO Utilizing Source-Combining Technique
item.description: This article presents a detailed investigation into optimizing the amplitude and phase of the transistor’s terminal voltages to generate a high 3rd-harmonic current in the millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) frequency. Based on the analysis, the digitally controlled source-combining triple-push (SCTP) oscillator is derived to significantly enhance the 3rd-harmonic current by introducing a large 3rd-harmonic component in the gate-to-source and drain-to-source voltages simultaneously. The analysis also aids in determining the resonant tank impedance and the output impedance. The proposed SCTP oscillator can achieve high output power and inherent rejection of 1st- and 2nd-subharmonic spurs without using multi-stage power- and area-hungry amplifiers or filters. Also, phase noise (PN) degradation due to the off-resonance oscillation in the triple-push oscillator is avoided by introducing auxiliary transconductance cells. Furthermore, the oscillator achieves high-frequency resolution by utilizing a linearized digital-to-current converter. Fabricated in 65-nm CMOS, the proposed 52.3-to-67.3-GHz SCTP oscillator prototype occupies a core area of 0.095 mm2 and consumes 24.8 to 32.8 mW. At a 60-GHz output frequency, the SCTP oscillator measures a PN of −126.17 dBc/Hz at 10 MHz, corresponding to a figure of merit (FoM) of 186.8 dBc/Hz. Benefited from a large frequency tuning range (TR) of 25.1%, the oscillator achieves the best-in-class FoMT at 1- and 10-MHz offsets. The measured frequency resolution is 35.8 kHz.

item.title: An Ultra-Low-Jitter Sampling-Filter-Based Charge-Pump PLL With Resistive-Discharge Time-Amplifying Phase-Frequency Detector and Series-Resonance VCO
item.description: This article presents a 13-GHz quadrature charge-pump phase-locked loop (CPPLL) that simultaneously achieves ultra-low jitter and low-spur performance. First, a low-noise resistive-discharge time-amplifying phase-frequency detector (RD-TAPFD) is proposed, achieving extremely low inherent noise and significantly suppressing noise from the following stages. Second, a sampling-based dual-path loop filter effectively suppresses reference spurs induced by charge-pump (CP) mismatch while maintaining a compact filter area. Third, a quadrature series-resonance voltage-controlled oscillator (SR-VCO) is implemented to minimize the out-of-band noise without the overvoltage issue. Fabricated in a 65-nm CMOS process, the CPPLL achieves an integrated rms jitter of 15.8 fs from 10 kHz to 100 MHz and a reference spur of −98.5 dBc while consuming 79.5 mW of power and achieving a jitter figure-of-merit (FoMJ) of −257 dB.

item.title: A 34 Gb/s 5 m DSP-Free PMF Active Cable in 22 nm FDSOI CMOS
item.description: This article presents a fully integrated transmit–receive wireline communication system based on a polymer microwave fiber (PMF) as a communication medium. Operating in the D-band (110–170 GHz), this system is based on coherent NRZ modulation and a non-coherent detection, including a phase-locked loop (PLL) for stable carrier generation and tunable millimeter-wave (mm-wave) and baseband (BB) transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) signal chains. The designed chips are fabricated in a 22 nm, fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FDSOI) CMOS technology and packaged in a flip-chip ball grid array (FCBGA) organic package with integrated in-package Vivaldi couplers. This system achieves a measured communication speed of 34 Gb/s at 5 m fiber length, without using any external digital equalization, with an energy efficiency of 1.7 pJ/bit/m and a bit error rate (BER) below 1e−8.

item.title: QVGA CMOS LiDAR Sensor With nMOS-Only SPAD Analog Front-End and Area-Efficient Priority Histogramming TDC
item.description: This article presents a high-resolution (HR) CMOS light detection and ranging (LiDAR) sensor capable of generating quarter video graphics array (QVGA) ( $320~{\times }~240$ ) depth images. To support high pixel density, the sensor employs a compact 6-transistor (6-T) nMOS-only single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) analog front-end (AFE) with a column-shared active recharge circuit. A two-step histogramming time-to-digital converter (hTDC) with a priority memory (PM) architecture is proposed to minimize memory usage. The PM scheme dynamically allocates additional memory only to histogram bins with a high likelihood of containing signal echoes. As a result, the hTDC achieves a 51% memory reduction compared to conventional two-step implementations, requiring only 188 bits per channel. The sensor supports two pixel configurations: a merging mode, which combines eight SPADs to produce a $160~{\times }~120$ image with enhanced sensitivity, and an HR mode, which uses two SPADs per macro pixel to generate a full-resolution $320~{\times }~240$ image. The prototype chip was fabricated using a 110-nm back-side illuminated (BSI) CMOS image sensor (CIS) process. The prototype sensor generates depth images at 10 frames/s in HR mode and 40 frames/s in merging mode. Under 100 klx ambient light, the sensor demonstrates a worst case depth error of 5.7 cm and a depth precision of 0.2% at a distance of 42 m.

item.title: A 16× Interleaved 32-GS/s 8b Hybrid ADC With Self-Tracking Inter-Stage Gain Achieving 44.3-dB SFDR at 20.9-GHz Input
item.description: This article presents a 32-GS/s 16-channel hierarchical time-interleaved (TI) hybrid analog-to-digital converter (ADC). The prototype utilizes the intrinsic high-speed quantization of time-domain (TD) ADC to reduce the interleaving factor. By incorporating hierarchical sampling and a cascode sampler, the compact TI-ADC achieves 44.3-dB spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) at 20.9-GHz input. The sub-ADC adopts a two-stage hybrid-domain architecture that combines a 3-bit successive approximation register (SAR) ADC with a 6-bit inverter-based opposite phase propagation (OPP) time-to-digital converter (TDC). A prototype chip is fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process, occupying a core area of 0.141 mm2. At 32 GS/s, it achieves a signal-to-noise and distortion ratio (SNDR) of 36 dB with a Nyquist input while consuming 142.3 mW, corresponding to a Walden figure-of-merit of 86.3 fJ/conv-step. Meanwhile, a delay-locked loop (DLL)-based calibration loop is proposed to calibrate the full-scale quantization range variation introduced by PVT variations, together with an analog self-tracking inter-stage gain calibration loop. The measured SNDR varies by 1.84 dB over a temperature range of $0~{^{\circ } }$ C to $100~{^{\circ } }$ C and fluctuates by 2.25 dB with a ±10% supply variation.

item.title: A 77-dB DR Two-Stage SAR ADC for Low-Gain Analog Front-Ends Using Asynchronous Pipelining and RC Snubber Reference Stabilization
item.description: The analog front-end (AFE) often bottlenecks the power of modern receiver chains, burdened by the large-signal linearity required before the ADC. This work introduces a 77-dB DR, 200-MS/s two-stage SAR ADC that can alleviate much of this burden by offering a significantly lower input-referred noise (IRN) to enable low-gain AFEs, while reaching conventionally challenging speeds. This level of performance is achieved via several circuit techniques, including domain-crossing RC reference snubbers that passively suppress voltage ringing, which in turn enables a noise-efficient, open-loop floating-inverter residue amplifier (RA). Furthermore, an asynchronous pipelining scheme is uniquely utilized to minimize idle time and to enhance the backend precision, while delivering an 8-ns, sample rate independent conversion latency. The 40-nm ADC prototype demonstrates a 10.9-nV/ $\surd $ Hz NSD for 5.8 mW at 200 MS/s, and with a 179.4-dB FoMS,DR, it surpasses the noise and speed of prior low-noise, SAR-based ADCs.

item.title: A Continuous-Time Zoom Sensor Readout Frontend With Fast Tracking and Floating-Gm-CCO Integrator
item.description: Emerging edge applications processing weak signals in noisy environments demand sensor readout frontends with low noise, low power, high dynamic range (DR), and high input impedance. This article presents a zoom sensor readout frontend design that can track signals with rapid changes over a wide DR with high energy efficiency. It employs a fast tracking technique that tracks input signals continuously by monitoring fine stage outputs. Relying on the fine stage result from a single conversion cycle, this technique greatly improves the tracking rate. To boost the energy efficiency of the fine stage, this work proposes a floating-Gm-CCO-based loop filter that allows an ultralow CCO operating voltage with a current-reused transconductance amplifier design. A prototype in a 28-nm CMOS achieves a 90.2-dB SNDR over a 10-kHz bandwidth with 4.91- $\mu \text {V}_{\text {rms}}$ input-referred noise and 4.82- $\mu $ W power consumption, yielding a Schreier FoM of 183.4 dB, the highest reported among low-noise sensor readout frontends.

item.title: A 760 mVPP-Input-Range, 103.6 dB-SNDR Direct-Digitization Sensor Readout With Pseudo-Differential Integrator and Impedance-Equalized RDAC
item.description: A high-precision, direct-digitization sensor readout (DD-RO) based on a continuous-time delta-sigma modulator (CT- $\Delta \Sigma $ M) is presented. The proposed DD-RO incorporates several key innovations to enhance performance. First, a pseudo-differential current-balancing integrator (PD-CBI) significantly extends the linear input range, whereas its intrinsically limited common-mode input range and CMRR are both improved by a common-mode cancellation loop (CMCL). Second, the PD-CBI enables quasi-quiet chopping for 1/ $f$ noise suppression and provides high input impedance. A multibit resistive DAC (RDAC) further increases the input impedance by reducing the transconductor’s net input voltage. Finally, an impedance-equalization technique employing auxiliary RDACs alleviates the signal-dependent nonlinearity arising from reference-path parasitics and DAC current variation. Fabricated in a 0.18- $\mu $ m CMOS process, the prototype achieves an input-referred noise (IRN) of 66 nV/ $\surd $ Hz, a 760 mVPP linear input range at 1.2 V supply, and a calibration-free input impedance of 7.83 G $\Omega $ and a CMRR of 82 dB, both measured at 50 Hz. The DD-RO achieves a peak SNDR of 103.6 dB and a dynamic range (DR) of 105 dB, corresponding to state-of-the-art figures of merit of FoM ${}_{\mathrm {SNDR}}= 173.5$ dB and FoM ${}_{\mathrm {DR}} = 174.9$ dB, respectively.

item.title: A 3.47 NEF 175.2-dB FoMs Direct Digitization Front-End Featuring Delta Amplification Noise-Shaping SAR ADC for Biosignal Acquisition
item.description: This article presents a direct-digitization interface for ExG bio-signals’ readout that simultaneously achieves a high dynamic range (DR) and a low noise-efficiency factor (NEF). The proposed delta amplification (DA) and feedback cancellation technique reduce both the input and output ranges of the first amplifier, thus allowing the use of a low NEF amplifier maximizing g ${}_{\textrm {m}}$ /I ${}_{\textrm {d}}$ while simultaneously enhancing wide DR. In addition, a small feedback capacitor in the proposed DA architecture significantly improves the noise gain, and a floating-inverter-based amplifier (FIA) is adopted to enhance the input impedance with superior energy efficiency. The prototype chip, fabricated in a 22-nm FDSOI process, consumes $4.62~{\mu }$ W with a signal bandwidth of 1 kHz and achieves an signal-to-noise-anddistortion ratio (SNDR) of 91.8 dB and a Schreier figure of merit (FoM ${}_{\textrm {S}}$ ) of 175.2 dB. The measured 3.47 NEF and 12.05 PEF are $1.9{\mathord {\times }}$ and $2.87{\mathord {\times }}$ smaller compared to prior art, respectively. Common mode rejection ratio is over 93 dB, and input impedance is 200 and 15 M $\Omega $ at DC and 1 kHz, respectively. To verify its robustness, the proposed interface is measured both in vitro and in vivo, including electrocardiography (ECG), electrooculography (EOG), electromyography (EMG), and electroencephalography (EEG) applications.

item.title: A MEMS-Free 4096-Pixel CMOS E-Nose Array With MOF-Based Molecular Selectivity, In-Pixel Thermal Regeneration, and a Compact Single-Coefficient Bandpass Sigma--Delta ADC
item.description: This work presents a CMOS-only [micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS)-free] electronic nose (e-nose) for concurrent multi-gas-sensing applications. The proposed system integrates 4096 capacitance-to-digital converter (CDC) pixels, each implementing a compact bandpass sigma–delta ( $\Sigma \Delta $ ) ADC with a single feedback coefficient and no additional feedforward or feedback paths, achieving each pixel footprint of only $45\times 45~\mu $ m. The e-nose can achieve full baseline recovery and sensor reusability through an in-pixel heater to enable rapid and complete desorption of gas molecules from the sensing surface. The chip also includes 128 temperature-sensing pixels for on-chip thermal monitoring, utilizing a bandgap-based temperature sensor followed by a hybrid active–passive $\Sigma \Delta $ ADC, maintaining the same compact pixel footprint as the CDC pixels. The system operates from a 1.1-V supply with a power consumption of $10.3~\mu $ W per pixel at a 1-MHz sampling rate. To achieve high molecular selectivity, metal–organic framework (MOF) materials are utilized as the sensing interface. Two MOFs: CoNi–Pyz and HKUST-1 are employed for selective detection of ammonia (NH3) and isopropyl alcohol (IPA), respectively, on the same chip. For NH3 sensing, the proposed e-nose achieves a limit of detection (LoD) of 5 ppm, a sensitivity of 0.012 ( $\Delta $ C/C)/ppm, and a wide sensing range from 5 to 1000 ppm. To the best of authors’ knowledge, this work achieves the highest reported density for a CMOS solid-state e-nose and represents the first demonstration of integrating both single and multiple MOF transducer materials directly on a CMOS chip. It also establishes a thermodynamically modulated sensing approach enabled by the in-pixel heater, ensuring full sensor reset and reusability.

item.title: A High-Linearity Shunt-Based In-Line Current Sensor With Self-Heating Compensation and 14.4 V 2 MHz PWM Rejection
item.description: This article presents a cost-effective, fully integrated shunt-resistor-based in-line current sensor that delivers high linearity and strong PWM rejection, enabling precise current measurement and control in dynamic driving systems like robotics, imaging, and audio. To mitigate the self-heating of the on-chip shunt resistor, which degrades linearity, a location-based thermal compensation technique is proposed. This technique reduces self-heating-induced distortion, improving THD+N by up to 23.6 dB over the full operating range without calibration. In addition, a floating transconductance (FG ${}_{\mathrm {m}}$ ) stage is introduced to reject the high dv/dt, high-voltage PWM components at the switching node of the power stage, enabling robust current sensing with this PWM common mode voltage. The prototype is implemented in a 180 nm BCD process and demonstrates a peak THD+N of–87.2 dB and a dynamic range (DR) of 89.1 dB. It achieves up to 2 MHz, 14.4 V PWM rejection with 2 V/ns $dv\mathrm {/}dt$ , and supports a ±6 A bidirectional current range.

item.title: GUARD: A Clock and Voltage Glitch Detector With On-Demand Protection
item.description: This article presents GUARD, a fully digital, variation-tolerant detector for clock and voltage glitch attacks, featuring an integrated on-demand protection mechanism. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS, GUARD provides robust security for digital systems by monitoring the system clock for maliciously injected faults. It employs a pair of optimized time-to-digital converters (TDCs) to detect clock pulsewidth variations as small as 100 ps and supports clock frequencies up to 1.2 GHz. Upon detection, a low-latency clock-gating mechanism is immediately triggered to prevent fault propagation into a victim microprocessor unit (MCU), achieving 100% protection success in experimental attacks. With simple one-time calibration, GUARD demonstrates robust operation across a wide industrial temperature range of $- 40~{^{\circ }}$ C to $125~{^{\circ }}$ C and a supply voltage range of 0.6 to 1.1 V. Furthermore, GUARD can differentiate between malicious voltage glitches and normal on-chip IR drops, thereby preventing unnecessary performance overhead. GUARD occupies $2958~\mu $ m2 and consumes 0.874 mW per 100 MHz of operating frequency.

item.title: A 36 V Current-Balancing Instrumentation Amplifier With ±24 V Input Range, 5.6 MHz BW, and 140 dB CMRR at All Gain Settings
item.description: This article presents a 36 V high-voltage current-balancing instrumentation amplifier (HV-CBIA), providing a new solution for industrial signal-acquisition front ends, including PLC input modules and motor drivers, where large input range, wide bandwidth, and high common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR) are simultaneously required. The proposed HV-CBIA addresses these requirements through three innovations: 1) a class-AB transconductance (TC) stage with adaptive biasing is proposed to extend the differential-mode (DM) input range while minimizing quiescent current; 2) a source-input buffer is employed to enhance the driving capability of transimpedance (TI) stage, while a negative capacitance (NC) technique is further incorporated to nullify parasitic capacitance, thereby improving the bandwidth–efficiency trade-off; and 3) an HV chopper employing area-efficient HV switches is adopted to maintain high CMRR and low offset under significant common-mode (CM) and DM swings. Fabricated in a 0.18- $\mu $ m BCD process, the proposed HV-CBIA achieves a ±24 V DM input signal range, 5.6 MHz bandwidth, and 140 dB CMRR across all gain settings (0.4-50). It delivers a 280 MHz gain–bandwidth product (GBW) at a gain of 50 while consuming only 0.7 mA from an 8–36 V supply, corresponding to a power efficiency of 400 MHz/mA.

item.title: A Single-Stage CSCR-Based SIDO/DISO Converter With Almost-Lossless Path Switching
item.description: This article introduces a single-stage single-input– dual-output/dual-input–single-output (SIDO/DISO) converter for autonomous Internet-of-Things (IoT) energy harvesting (EH), utilizing a continuously scalable-conversion-ratio (CSCR) topology. By adopting time-multiplexing control (TMC) instead of ordered-power-distribution control (OPDC), the design achieves independent regulation of input and output voltages and decouples the step-up/step-down characteristics of the two power paths. To minimize path-switching power loss caused by flying capacitor voltage ( $\boldsymbol {V}_{\mathrm { CF}}$ ) variations under TMC, this work combines idle-cell operation with reconfigurable $\boldsymbol {V}_{\mathrm { CF}}$ step sizing. In addition, a phase-parity alignment technique is employed to prevent phase degeneration during path switching. Fabricated in 65-nm CMOS, the prototype demonstrates peak efficiencies of 91.4% (SIDO) and 92.6% (DISO), with less than 2% efficiency drop as the path-switching frequency increases from 50 to 625 kHz.

item.title: A 95.3% Efficiency APT/AET/SPT Multimode Multiband CMOS/GaN Envelope Tracking for 6G-Oriented Systems
item.description: This article proposes an envelope-tracking (ET) supply modulator (SM) that is scalable for sixth-generation (6G) communication systems. The design leverages a cost-efficient CMOS process for the power converters and a high-performance GaN process for the high-frequency power amplifier (PA) and the depletion-mode-only GaN-based amplifier. The proposed ET supply modulator (ETSM) supports average power tracking (APT), Analog ET (AET), and symbol power tracking (SPT) operation modes, achieving 400 MHz ET bandwidth and up to 95.3% efficiency, while also enabling fast mode transitions. Parasitic-induced voltage ringing in SPT mode is effectively mitigated by activating the depletion-mode-only GaN-based class-AB amplifier as an active snubber, maintaining performance despite parasitic variations. This solution overcomes the limitations of existing techniques and provides robust performance across multimode-multiband (MMMB) operation, spanning 2G to 5G FR2 and beyond. Experimental results demonstrate high efficiency, rapid mode transitions, and substantial mitigation of parasitic voltage ringing.

item.title: A 6.78-MHz Single-Stage Regulating Rectifier With Dual Outputs Simultaneously Charged in a Half Cycle Achieving 92.2% Efficiency and 131 mW Output Power
item.description: Targeting the wireless power transfer (WPT) to implantable medical devices (IMDs), this work presents a 6.78 MHz single-stage dual-output (SSDO) regulating rectifier. It can support the simultaneous charging of both outputs ( $V_{\text {OUT1}}$ and $V_{\text {OUT2}}$ , $V_{\text {OUT1}} \gt V_{\text {OUT2}}$ ) in a half cycle, rather than in the conventional time-multiplexing manner, which can effectively boost the load power ( $P_{\text {OUT}}$ ) and power conversion efficiency ( $\eta _{\text {REC}}$ ). This rectifier was implemented using only three NMOS active diodes to minimize power loss that would otherwise be caused by PMOS. Furthermore, we proposed a charge distribution (CD) mode that can eliminate a large drop in voltage when $V_{\text {OUT2}}$ is under a heavy load condition. The proposed SSDO rectifier was fabricated in a 180 nm CMOS process and occupied a chip area of 1.63 mm2. Measurement results verified two regulated outputs ( $V_{\text {OUT1}} =3.3$ V, $V_{\text {OUT2}}$ ranges from 1.3 to 1.6 V) even under the strict case where $V_{\text {OUT1}}$ and $V_{\text {OUT2}}$ simultaneously transition from light to heavy conditions. Owing to the proposed simultaneous charging concept as well as the implementation topology, the rectifier supports a peak $P_{\text {OUT}}$ of 131 mW and a peak $\eta _{\text {REC}}$ of 92.2%. The performances achieved were competitive compared with prior SSDO rectifiers.

item.title: An Ultralow Cross-Regulation Single-Inductor Multiple-Output (SIMO) Buck Converter Using Reordered Power-Distributive Control
item.description: A single-inductor multiple-output (SIMO) buck converter employing reordered power-distributive control (RPDC) is presented to achieve ultralow cross regulation. A dedicated power-distribution controller implements RPDC by adaptively adjusting the switching sequence: when the inductor current is insufficient, the switching period is extended, and when excessive, an end phase in the form of a freewheeling phase is inserted to minimize cross regulation. During large transients, RPDC is activated; aided by transient detection and processing (TDP), the controller prioritizes victim outputs and defers transient outputs to the end phase, thereby further suppressing cross regulation without hurting the transient outputs. The converter, fabricated in a 0.18- $\mu $ m BCD process with all power transistors integrated on-chip, demonstrates a measured voltage droop of 188 mV and cross regulation of 9 mV/A in the worst-case scenario under a 2-A load transient. Without the freewheeling period in the steady state, the converter achieves a peak efficiency of 89.6% at 2.7 W.

item.title: A Radiated-EMI-Suppressed Isolated DC--DC Converter With Complementary Edge-Aligned and Adaptive Over-Compensation Techniques
item.description: This article presents a 5-to-5-V isolated DC–DC converter that suppresses radiated electromagnetic interference (EMI) using two control loops on symmetric transmitter/receiver (TX/RX) full-bridge stages. A complementary edge-aligned loop is implemented at the TX side to minimize fluctuations in the primary-side common-mode voltage (V ${}_{\mathrm {\!CM\_P}})$ during inverter switching transitions. An adaptive over-compensation loop is applied at the RX side to suppress secondary-side common-mode voltage (V ${}_{\mathrm {\!CM\_S}})$ fluctuation by enabling early turn-off near the zero-current crossing. These techniques directly reduce common-mode current (I ${}_{\mathrm {CM}})$ without relying on frequency hopping or external EMI suppression components. The transformer and feedback isolation capacitors are co-integrated in a four-layer low-cost package substrate and assembled with the TX and RX dies—fabricated in a 0.18- $\mu $ m BCD process—into a land grid array (LGA) package. The prototype achieves a peak efficiency of 60% and a maximum output power (P ${}_{\mathrm {OUT}})$ of 2.1 W. The system complies with CISPR-32 Class B radiated EMI limits on a two-layer PCB without using stitching capacitors or external beads.

item.title: One-Cycle-Balance Control in Buck Converters for Consecutive Load-Step Events
item.description: One-cycle-balance (OCB) response represents the optimal load-transient response for buck converters, maximizing system energy efficiency and robustness. While prior art has demonstrated OCB response for single load-step events, it fails in consecutive transients, which are prevalent in modern applications. This work overcomes these limitations by introducing an OCB controller that achieves a near-optimal response at every stage of a consecutive transient event sequence. The controller employs a polygon timer for one-cycle compensation of the accumulated charge imbalance. A relay emulated curve (REC) method achieves reduced-complexity sensing of the critical timing, independent of load current profiles in consecutive events. Moreover, a differentiator-based transient detector with dynamic boundaries successfully detects the onset of each transient event with low latency. Fabricated in a 0.18- $\mu $ m BCD process, a prototype demonstrates a nearly ideal OCB response, with a deviation-from-ideal (DFI) rate of less than 7.8% across various single and consecutive events.

item.title: A 6.9-ppm/°C, 0.66-mV/V Line Regulation, 50-mA Multi-Loop Low-Dropout Regulator With Integrated Single-BJT Voltage and Current References
item.description: This article presents a fully integrated output-capacitor-less (OCL) multi-feedback-loop low-dropout regulator (LDO) with an in-built single bipolar junction transistor (BJT)-based voltage and current reference (VCR) for energy-harvesting Internet of Things (IoT) devices. The proposed architecture comprises four loops, which significantly enhance the DC regulation and transient performance of the LDO. A tri-loop regulation core based on a flipped-voltage-follower (FVF) structure offers high DC loop gain, resulting in enhanced line and load regulation. A replica-based slew-rate enhancement (RSRE) loop improves the undershoot and overshoot recovery times during load transient response. Furthermore, the proposed LDO consumes less area and power, and exhibits reduced output noise by integrating a single-BJT branch bandgap reference (BGR) with an FVF power stage, unlike conventional LDOs that use externally connected BGRs, which require multiple resistors and BJTs. The bias current is generated internally by a proposed current reference (CR) based on a shared single-BJT and is powered by the LDO output voltage to improve current line sensitivity (LS). The proposed design is fabricated in a 65-nm low-power (LP) CMOS technology and occupies an area of 0.041 mm2. The proposed LDO delivers a maximum load current of 50 mA at a nominal output voltage of 1.2 V. Measurement results show that the proposed LDO achieves line and load regulation of 0.66 mV/V and 0.195 mV/mA, respectively. The measured average temperature coefficients (TCs) of the output voltage and bias reference current are 6.9 and 86.55 ppm/°C, respectively, over $- 40~^{\circ } $ C to $85~^{\circ } $ C, with corresponding voltage and current accuracies ( $\sigma /\mu $ ) of 0.16% and 1.42%. The measured power supply rejection (PSR) at 10 Hz is 67.5 dB at maximum load current. The proposed LDO consumes a 268-nA quiescent current at room temperature with a minimum supply voltage of 1.3 V. We achieve a transient figure of merit of 1.27 fs.

item.title: A Complementary Positive Feedback-Assisted Current Mirror-Based Level Shifter for Energy-Efficient Level Conversion for Wide Voltage Ranges
item.description: A complementary positive feedback-assisted current mirror-based level shifter (CPFLS) is proposed to reliably convert subthreshold signals to higher voltages. By adopting a positive feedback structure, the CPFLS mitigates the delay degradation and short-circuit current issues inherent in a prior art, WCMLS, due to its negative feedback design. Additionally, the CPFLS addresses the instability caused by the dynamic node in the CMLS-LED by incorporating a current-limiting circuit. Moreover, the CPFLS effectively prevents the delay degradation observed in diode-MOSFET insertion-type LSs with split-controlled inverter, when the voltage difference between the input and output is small, leveraging its positive feedback structure to maintain fast and stable operation. The measurement results from a test chip fabricated in 28-nm CMOS technology demonstrate that the CPFLS successfully converts a 0.28-V input signal to a 1.0-V nominal voltage with stable operation, achieving an 89% improvement in the measured delay compared to WCMLS. Furthermore, the CPFLS achieves up to 53%/75% faster measured delay and 63%/89% better energy-delay product (EDP) than the split-level converter (SLC) at V ${}_{\mathrm {DDH}} = 1.0$ /0.7 V, respectively.

item.title: A Highly Integrated Primary-Side Zero-Voltage Switching Active Clamp Flyback Control IC for a 5-cm3 5-V/1-A AC–DC Converter With Adaptive Frequency and Deadtime Control
item.description: This article presents a miniaturized 5-W output AC–DC converter for Internet of Things (IoT) and smart building powered by wall power. The implemented control IC for an active clamp flyback (ACF) AC–DC converter achieves up to 500-kHz switching operation to reduce passive elements compared to conventional passive clamp flyback and secondary-side regulation flyback converters. Toward further miniaturization of the system, the implemented IC can support adaptive frequency control and zero-voltage switching (ZVS) without high-voltage (HV) components. The chip can adaptively operate from 300- to over 500-kHz switching frequency with dynamic deadtime control techniques. This work reduces the magnetizing inductance of the transformer by 60% compared to previous works, down $85~{\mathrm {\mu \text {H} }}$ . The full AC–DC system volume occupies 4.99 cm3, which is 50% smaller than prior works, and achieves a power density of 1.00 W/cm3 at 5 V/1 A from 85- to 265-Vac input with a peak efficiency of 81.0%.

item.title: A 0.4-V 988-nW Tiny Footprint Time-Domain Audio Feature Extraction ASIC for Keyword Spotting Using Injection-Locked Oscillators
item.description: This work presents an injection-locked oscillator (ILO)-based feature extraction (FEx) system. It combines voltage- and time-domain signal processing to implement a power-efficient programmable gain amplifier (PGA) and a small-footprint, high-selectivity ILO-based voltage-to-time converter bandpass filter (VTC-BPF) bank and rectifier. The VTC-BPF enables direct analog-to-time conversion, eliminating the need for a separate VTC stage, and allows compact full-wave rectification via an xor gate. Fabricated in 65-nm CMOS, the prototype occupies 0.15 mm, 3.5 smaller than recent designs, while consuming 988 nW, making it 9 more power-efficient than existing fully time-domain solution. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first silicon-verified analog FEx operating at 0.4 V, achieving 86.3% accuracy on a 12-class keyword spotting (KWS) task.

item.title: Denim: Heterogeneous Compute-in-Memory Accelerator Exploiting Denoising--Similarity for Diffusion Models
item.description: Diffusion models have recently revolutionized the field of image synthesis due to their ability to generate photorealistic images. However, one of the main drawbacks of diffusion models is that the image generation process is expensive. Large image-to-image networks have to be applied multiple times in order to iteratively optimize the least altered noised image across steps. We investigate the behavior of layers during the denoising process, and find that the changes between steps are generally very small. Leveraging this characteristic called denoising--similarity in this article, we perform differential computing on the input data to resolve such computational redundancy and improve hardware efficiency. At the algorithm level, we perform mix-precision quantization on the input differences within the same layer, so that the original floating-point (FP) computation can be divided into dense INT computation and sparse FP computation. At the hardware level, we propose a heterogeneous compute-in-memory (CIM) accelerator with three design features. First, a sign-magnitude (SM) radix-8 Booth CIM macro that utilizes a hybrid encoding strategy is designed to reduce cycle count and power consumption on bitwise multiplications. Second, a four-operand exponent CIM (4Op-ECIM) macro, activating four bitcells per column for dual additions, integrates mantissa processing engines to efficiently process FP data without exponent alignment or repeated mantissa access. Third, the 4Op-ECIM is designed to be reconfigurable as a binary content-addressable memory (CAM) for identifying the sparse FP computations, thereby preventing its redundant bitline precharging and sensing operations. The 28-nm fabricated chip shows 67.89 TFLOPS/W@FP16 and 74.34 TFLOPS/W@BF16 system energy efficiency on the tested diffusion models.

item.title: Falcon: Event-Driven Hybrid Object Tracking SoC With Bit-Column-Similarity-Based MRAM PIM and Heterogeneous Read-Only-Once Attention Flow
item.description: Hybrid frame-event cameras offer high spatial fidelity and $\mu $ s-level temporal response, making them well suited for low-power, low-latency object tracking under motion blur and sparse activity. This work presents an event-driven vision SoC that integrates heterogeneous MRAM-based processing-in-memory (PIM), near-memory-computing (NMC), lookup table (LUT), and single-instruction multiple-data (SIMD) compute units for end-to-end real-time hybrid tracking. First, the CNN feature encoder is mapped onto a bit-column-similarity-optimized MRAM PIM with activation skipping and weight compression, achieving $2.44\times $ energy efficiency and 61.9% latency reduction. Second, attention-based tracking is executed using a read-once $Q$ / $K$ / $V$ dataflow combining column-priority NMC generation, mixed-product SIMD execution, and LUT-accelerated SoftMax, reducing buffer reads by 46% and attention latency by 30%. Third, a two-stage event-driven activation pipeline selectively enables computation only upon motion, cutting system power by 63.5% and overall latency by 68.8%. Fabricated in 28-nm FDSOI (12.96 mm2), the SoC delivers macro-level 750.18 TOPS/W for 1b–1b–3b MAC operations at 0.7 V, 50 MHz, and system-level 16.34 TOPS/W for INT8 CNN + FP8 attention at 1.15 V, 200 MHz, enabling real-time 50 frames/p tracking at 196.5-mW power consumption.

item.title: ASAP: A 28-nm Transformer Training Accelerator With Alternating Sparsity and Asymmetrical Microscaling Precision
item.description: This work presents ASAP, a 28-nm transformer-training accelerator that combines N:M structured sparsity with asymmetric microscaling floating-point (MXFP) precision through a unified algorithm–hardware co-design. ASAP introduces a progressive sparsity schedule in which pruned compute resources are reassigned to increase numerical precision for important weights and activations, stabilizing optimization while reducing overall computation. A placement-aware N:M reordering mechanism aligns partial products within each processing element, minimizing shift distances, lowering toggle activity, and sustaining utilization across sparsity levels. To address the performance bottleneck of nonlinear (NL) layers, a reconfigurable pipeline single-instruction multiple-data (SIMD) engine supports various NL functions and their gradients through a scatter-network datapath, achieving up to $3.4\times $ throughput improvement. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS, ASAP attains 22.4 TOPS/W peak efficiency and delivers 2.02– $5.07\times $ higher end-to-end training energy efficiency than prior training processors, while preserving FP32-level accuracy on MAE ViT-B and BERT workloads. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of coordinated sparsity–precision scheduling and placement-aware dataflow for future energy-efficient transformer-training accelerators.

item.title: PROTEUS: A 40 nm Programmable General-Purpose Digital Compute-In-Memory Accelerator With eNVM and Hierarchical ISA for Versatile Edge AI
item.description: We present PROTEUS, an 18 mm2 programmable general-purpose digital compute-in-memory (GP-DCIM) accelerator integrating 4 Mb resistive random access memory (RRAM) and 2.6 Mb tensor static random access memory (SRAM) with a 32-bit hierarchical DCIM instruction set architecture (ISA). PROTEUS features fine-grained 1-D matrix tiling and a reconfigurable DCIM datapath/pipeline for near-100% memory utilization, supporting INT8/INT16/FP8/FP16 DCIM computations. PROTEUS unifies SRAM/RRAM dataflows and embeds nonvolatile micro-programs in RRAM to enable rapid switching among prestored kernels without incurring off-chip instruction feeds or RRAM rewrites. Fabricated in 40 nm ultra-low power (ULP) CMOS with foundry RRAM, PROTEUS delivers 702 GOPS throughput, 6.4 TOPS/W energy efficiency, and 0.039 TOPS/mm2 compute density. It is validated on ResNet-20, BERT-Tiny, MobileViT, GraphSAGE, and Vision Mamba, demonstrating versatility across CNN, Transformer, hybrid CNN-Transformer, graph neural network (GNN), and state-space model (SSM) workloads.

item.title: A BEV Perception Transformer Accelerator With Saliency-Driven Image/Point Cloud Fusion and Phase-Linked Dataflow in 28 nm CMOS
item.description: Deploying advanced Transformer-based models for real-time, high-accuracy multimodal bird’s-eye-view (BEV) perception in autonomous driving imposes substantial hardware demands. To address this, we propose a low-cost, low-power image/point-cloud fusion Transformer accelerator that supports two modes: high-performance driving and ultra-low-power sentry operation. We first propose a cross-modal saliency evaluation mechanism that prunes redundant computation. We then propose a column-wise computing array with a three-level adaptive-precision strategy to enable saliency-driven fusion.
